    TableSheet¶

    Guides: Getting started.

    Class¶

    TableSheet ¶

    Bases: PanelMixin, StylingMixin, LayoutMixin, OutputMixin

    Build an institutional image from one or several styled tables.

    The sheet holds the DataFrames, records the styling you apply to each one, and composes everything (titles, notes, sources) into a single image. Like GraphMtplt, every method returns the sheet, so calls can be chained.

    How it works
    • Each table is a recipe: its source plus the ordered list of operations applied through the styling methods. The Styler is rebuilt from the recipe whenever needed, so re-running a notebook cell never accumulates CSS.
    • Tables are rendered by a headless browser, all in one batch, and cached by content: changing a title, the layout or the spacing never renders again; changing one table renders only that table.
    • Panels (tables and charts) are arranged on a grid (layout) that can span rows and columns, and positioned with subplots_adjust.
    • preview() shows the result in the notebook, save() writes it.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    dataframe DataFrame | Styler | Series | Mapping | Sequence | None

    One table, a list of tables, or a {name: table} mapping. More can be added later with add_table. The first panel is active.

    		 None
    names Sequence[str] | None

    Panel names for a list input. Defaults to "panel_<n>".

    		 None
    style SheetStyle | None

    Base visual parameters.

    		 None
    renderer Callable | None

    renderer(documents, dpi) -> images. Defaults to PlaywrightRenderer().

    		 None
    cache RenderCache | None

    Cache of rendered tables. None uses the process-wide cache shared by every sheet; RenderCache(max_mb=0) disables caching.

    		 None
    nrows int | None

    Shape of the grid the panels are placed on, in creation order. nrows=1 puts the panels side by side, ncols=1 (the default) stacks them. See layout for explicit arrangements.

    		 None
    ncols int | None

    Shape of the grid the panels are placed on, in creation order. nrows=1 puts the panels side by side, ncols=1 (the default) stacks them. See layout for explicit arrangements.

    		 None
    width_ratios Sequence[float] | None

    Relative width of every grid column.

    		 None
    **style_options Unpack[SheetStyleOptions]

    Any SheetStyle field, e.g. width_in=11 or height_in=7.5.

    		 {}

    Examples:

    One table.

    >>> sheet = (
...     TableSheet(df, width_in=7)
...     .style_table(font_size=11, text_align="center")
...     .format("{:.0f}")
...     .panel(title="Δ Yield", subtitle="Basis points")
...     .add_source("Fuente: Example Data")
... )
>>> sheet.preview()
>>> sheet.save("yield.png")

    Two tables side by side and a chart that spans both rows on the right.

    >>> sheet = (
...     TableSheet({"yield": df_yield, "spreads": df_spreads}, width_in=13)
...     .on().style_table(font_size=11, text_align="center")      # both
...     .on("yield").panel(title="Δ Yield")
...     .on("spreads").panel(title="Δ Spreads")
...     .add_image(graph, name="curve").panel(title="Yield curve")
...     .layout([["yield", "curve"], ["spreads", "curve"]], width_ratios=[3, 2])
...     .subplots_adjust(wspace=0.1, hspace=0.2)
...     .add_title("Renta fija local")
...     .add_source("Fuente: Example Data")
...     .save(dir="out", name="lamina")
... )

    class TableSheet(PanelMixin, StylingMixin, LayoutMixin, OutputMixin):
    """
    Build an institutional image from one or several styled tables.

    The sheet holds the DataFrames, records the styling you apply to each
    one, and composes everything (titles, notes, sources) into a single
    image. Like ``GraphMtplt``, every method returns the sheet, so calls
    can be chained.

    How it works
    ------------
    * Each table is a *recipe*: its source plus the ordered list of
      operations applied through the styling methods. The ``Styler`` is
      rebuilt from the recipe whenever needed, so re-running a notebook
      cell never accumulates CSS.
    * Tables are rendered by a headless browser, **all in one batch**, and
      cached by content: changing a title, the layout or the spacing never
      renders again; changing one table renders only that table.
    * Panels (tables and charts) are arranged on a grid (``layout``) that
      can span rows and columns, and positioned with ``subplots_adjust``.
    * ``preview()`` shows the result in the notebook, ``save()`` writes it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dataframe : DataFrame | Styler | Series | Mapping | Sequence | None, default None
        One table, a list of tables, or a ``{name: table}`` mapping. More
        can be added later with ``add_table``. The first panel is active.
    names : Sequence[str] | None, default None
        Panel names for a list input. Defaults to ``"panel_<n>"``.
    style : SheetStyle | None, default None
        Base visual parameters.
    renderer : Callable | None, default None
        ``renderer(documents, dpi) -> images``. Defaults to
        ``PlaywrightRenderer()``.
    cache : RenderCache | None, default None
        Cache of rendered tables. ``None`` uses the process-wide cache
        shared by every sheet; ``RenderCache(max_mb=0)`` disables caching.
    nrows, ncols : int | None, default None
        Shape of the grid the panels are placed on, in creation order.
        ``nrows=1`` puts the panels side by side, ``ncols=1`` (the
        default) stacks them. See ``layout`` for explicit arrangements.
    width_ratios : Sequence[float] | None, default None
        Relative width of every grid column.
    **style_options
        Any ``SheetStyle`` field, e.g. ``width_in=11`` or ``height_in=7.5``.

    Examples
    --------
    One table.

    >>> sheet = (
    ...     TableSheet(df, width_in=7)
    ...     .style_table(font_size=11, text_align="center")
    ...     .format("{:.0f}")
    ...     .panel(title="Δ Yield", subtitle="Basis points")
    ...     .add_source("Fuente: Example Data")
    ... )
    >>> sheet.preview()
    >>> sheet.save("yield.png")

    Two tables side by side and a chart that spans both rows on the right.

    >>> sheet = (
    ...     TableSheet({"yield": df_yield, "spreads": df_spreads}, width_in=13)
    ...     .on().style_table(font_size=11, text_align="center")      # both
    ...     .on("yield").panel(title="Δ Yield")
    ...     .on("spreads").panel(title="Δ Spreads")
    ...     .add_image(graph, name="curve").panel(title="Yield curve")
    ...     .layout([["yield", "curve"], ["spreads", "curve"]], width_ratios=[3, 2])
    ...     .subplots_adjust(wspace=0.1, hspace=0.2)
    ...     .add_title("Renta fija local")
    ...     .add_source("Fuente: Example Data")
    ...     .save(dir="out", name="lamina")
    ... )
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        dataframe: TableLike | Mapping[str, TableLike] | Sequence[TableLike] | None = None,
        *,
        names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
        style: SheetStyle | None = None,
        renderer: Renderer | None = None,
        cache: RenderCache | None = None,
        nrows: int | None = None,
        ncols: int | None = None,
        width_ratios: Sequence[float] | None = None,
        **style_options: Unpack[SheetStyleOptions],
    ) -> None:
        self._panels = []
        self._active = []
        self._style = style or SheetStyle()
        self._header: Header | None = None
        self._notes = []
        self._sources = []
        self._mosaic = None
        self._shape = None
        self._width_ratios = None
        self._renderer = renderer or PlaywrightRenderer()
        self._cache = DEFAULT_CACHE if cache is None else cache
        self._counter = 0
        self._last_path: Path | None = None

        if style_options:
            self.config_layout(**style_options)

        for name, table in self._normalize_input(dataframe, names):
            self.add_table(table, name=name, activate=False)

        if self._panels:
            self._active = [self._panels[0].name]

        if nrows is not None or ncols is not None or width_ratios is not None:
            self.layout(nrows=nrows, ncols=ncols, width_ratios=width_ratios)

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_input(
        dataframe: object,
        names: Sequence[str] | None,
    ) -> list[tuple[str | None, TableLike]]:
        """Return ``(name, table)`` pairs for every accepted input shape."""
        if dataframe is None:
            if names:
                raise ValueError("names given without any dataframe.")
            return []

        if isinstance(dataframe, (DataFrame, Styler, Series)):
            items = [dataframe]
        elif isinstance(dataframe, Mapping):
            if names is not None:
                raise TypeError(
                    "names cannot be used with a mapping; its keys are "
                    "the panel names."
                )
            return [(str(key), value) for key, value in dataframe.items()]
        else:
            items = list(dataframe)  # type: ignore[call-overload]

        if names is None:
            return [(None, item) for item in items]

        if len(names) != len(items):
            raise ValueError(
                f"names has {len(names)} entries for {len(items)} tables."
            )
        return list(zip(names, items))

    def _find(self, key: Key) -> Panel:
    """
    Return the panel referenced by a position or a name.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the position or name does not exist.
    TypeError
        If ``key`` is neither ``int`` nor ``str``.
    """
    if isinstance(key, bool) or not isinstance(key, (int, str)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"A panel key must be an int position or a str name, "
            f"got {type(key).__name__}."
        )

    if isinstance(key, int):
        try:
            return self._panels[key]
        except IndexError:
            raise KeyError(
                f"Panel position {key} is out of range "
                f"(0..{len(self._panels) - 1})."
            ) from None

    for panel in self._panels:
        if panel.name == key:
            return panel

    raise KeyError(
        f"Unknown panel {key!r}. Available: "
        f"{[panel.name for panel in self._panels]}."
    )

    def _targets(self, *, tables_only: bool = False) -> list[Panel]:
    """
    Return the active panels.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tables_only : bool, default False
        Require every active panel to be a table.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the sheet has no panels.
    TypeError
        If ``tables_only`` and an active panel is an image.
    """
    if not self._panels:
        raise ValueError(
            "The sheet has no panels. Add one with add_table() or "
            "add_image()."
        )

    panels = [self._find(name) for name in self._active]

    if tables_only:
        images = [p.name for p in panels if p.kind != "table"]
        if images:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Styling applies to tables only; image panels are "
                f"active: {images}. Use on(...) to select tables."
            )

    return panels

    def _resolve_grid(self) -> GridLayout:
    """
    Return the grid of the sheet.

    An explicit layout is used as it is (panels added after it was set
    are left out, with a warning); otherwise the panels are placed in
    creation order according to ``nrows`` / ``ncols``.
    """
    if not self._panels:
        raise ValueError(
            "The sheet has no panels. Add one with add_table() or "
            "add_image()."
        )

    if self._mosaic is not None:
        grid = GridLayout(self._mosaic, self._width_ratios)
        left_out = [
            name for name in self.panel_names if name not in grid.spans
        ]
        if left_out:
            warnings.warn(
                f"Panels not placed in the layout and left out: "
                f"{left_out}.",
                stacklevel=3,
            )
        return grid

    nrows, ncols = self._shape or (None, None)
    return GridLayout.filled(
        self.panel_names, nrows, ncols, self._width_ratios
    )

    def _visible_panels(self, grid: GridLayout) -> list[Panel]:
    by_name = {panel.name: panel for panel in self._panels}
    return [by_name[name] for name in grid.spans]

    def _rasterize(self, panels: Iterable[Panel]) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Return the RGB image of every given panel.

    Tables are looked up in the cache by content. Everything that is
    missing is rendered in a single batch (one browser launch).
    """
    style = self._style
    token = getattr(
        self._renderer, "cache_token", type(self._renderer).__qualname__
    )

    images: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
    key_of: dict[str, str] = {}
    pending: dict[str, str] = {}

    for panel in panels:
        if panel.kind == "image":
            images[panel.name] = rasterize_image(panel.source, style.dpi)
            continue

        document = build_document(
            panel.build_styler().to_html(),
            font_px=style.table_font_px,
            zebra=style.zebra,
        )
        key = make_key(token, style.dpi, document)
        key_of[panel.name] = key

        cached = self._cache.get(key)
        if cached is not None:
            images[panel.name] = cached
        else:
            pending.setdefault(key, document)

    if pending:
        rendered = list(self._renderer(list(pending.values()), style.dpi))
        if len(rendered) != len(pending):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The renderer returned {len(rendered)} images for "
                f"{len(pending)} documents."
            )

        fresh: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for key, image in zip(pending, rendered):
            fresh[key] = array_to_rgb(image)
            self._cache.put(key, fresh[key])

        for name, key in key_of.items():
            if name not in images:
                images[name] = fresh[key]

    return images

    def render(self) -> Self:
    """
    Pre-render the tables.

    Renders (or fetches from the cache) the image of every visible
    table so that ``preview``, ``save`` and the other outputs are
    immediate afterwards. It is optional: those methods render on
    demand.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.
    """
    self._rasterize(self._visible_panels(self._resolve_grid()))
    return self

    ----------
    fmt : {"png", "pdf", "svg", "jpg"}, default "png"
        Output format. ``png`` bytes can be inserted directly into a
        presentation, e.g. ``io.BytesIO(sheet.to_bytes())``.
    transparent : bool, default False
        Transparent background.

    Returns
    -------
    bytes
        Encoded image.
    """
    fmt = fmt.lower().lstrip(".")
    if fmt not in _FORMATS:
        raise ValueError(f"fmt must be one of {sorted(_FORMATS)}.")

    fig = self.figure
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    # 'standard' bbox keeps the computed size even if the user has
    # ``savefig.bbox = "tight"`` in their matplotlib configuration.
    with matplotlib.rc_context({"savefig.bbox": "standard"}):
        fig.savefig(
            buffer,
            format="jpeg" if fmt == "jpg" else fmt,
            dpi=self._style.dpi,
            facecolor="none" if transparent else self._style.background,
            transparent=transparent,
        )
    return buffer.getvalue()

    def to_array(self) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Return the sheet as an RGB ``uint8`` array ``(H, W, 3)``.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Pixels of the final image.
    """
    fig = self.figure
    fig.canvas.draw()
    return np.asarray(fig.canvas.buffer_rgba())[..., :3].copy()

    def save(
    self,
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    dir: str | Path | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
    fmt: str | None = None,
    transparent: bool = False,
) -> Self:
    """
    Write the sheet to a file.

    Give either ``path`` or ``name`` (with an optional ``dir``), as in
    ``GraphMtplt.save``. The format comes from ``fmt`` or from the file
    extension (``png`` when there is none).

    Parameters
    ----------
    path : str | pathlib.Path | None, default None
        Complete output path.
    dir : str | pathlib.Path | None, default None
        Output folder (created if missing). Used with ``name``.
    name : str | None, default None
        File name, with or without extension.
    fmt : {"png", "pdf", "svg", "jpg"} | None, default None
        Output format. Overrides the extension.
    transparent : bool, default False
        Transparent background.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining. See ``last_path``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If neither ``path`` nor ``name`` is given, or ``fmt`` is not
        supported.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.save("out/lamina.png")
    >>> sheet.save(dir="out", name="lamina", fmt="pdf")
    """
    if path is None and name is None:
        raise ValueError("Give either path or name.")

    target = Path(path) if path is not None else Path(dir or ".") / name

    suffix = target.suffix.lstrip(".").lower()
    chosen = (fmt or suffix or "png").lower().lstrip(".")
    if chosen not in _FORMATS:
        raise ValueError(f"fmt must be one of {sorted(_FORMATS)}.")
    if suffix != chosen:
        # Replace a known image extension, append to anything else.
        target = (
            target.with_suffix(f".{chosen}")
            if suffix in _FORMATS
            else target.with_name(f"{target.name}.{chosen}")
        )

    data = self.to_bytes(chosen, transparent=transparent)

    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(data)
    self._last_path = target
    return self

    def preview(self) -> Self:
    """
    Display the sheet in a Jupyter notebook without writing a file.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.
    """
    try:
        from IPython import get_ipython
        from IPython.display import Image, display
    except ImportError:
        get_ipython = None

    if get_ipython is None or get_ipython() is None:
        warnings.warn(
            "preview() only displays inside IPython/Jupyter.",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return self

    display(Image(data=self.to_bytes("png"), format="png"))
    return self

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
    if self._mosaic is not None:
        layout = f"layout={self._mosaic}"
    elif self._shape is not None:
        layout = f"nrows={self._shape[0]}, ncols={self._shape[1]}"
    else:
        layout = "stacked"
    return (
        f"{type(self).__name__}("
        f"panels={[p.name for p in self._panels]}, "
        f"active={self._active}, "
        f"{layout}, width_in={self._style.width_in})"
    )

    """
    Append general notes below the panels (above the sources).

    Parameters
    ----------
    *notes : str | Sequence[str]
        One or several notes.
    size : float | None, default None
        Font size in points of **all** notes: the general ones and the
        ones under each panel. ``None`` leaves the current size
        unchanged (``footer_size`` unless it was set before). To go

    ------
    ValueError
        If ``size`` is not positive. Nothing is changed in that case.

    Examples
    --------

    for note in notes:
        self._notes.extend(_as_list(note))
    return self

    def config_layout(self, **changes: Unpack[SheetStyleOptions]) -> Self:
    """
    Change visual parameters of the sheet.

    Parameters
    ----------
    **changes
        Any ``SheetStyle`` field: ``width_in``, ``height_in``,
        ``dpi``, ``left``, ``wspace``, ``line_width``, ``scale``,
        ``font_family``... Fields that accept ``None`` (``height_in``,
        ``left``, ``right``, ``bottom``, ``top``, ``wspace``,
        ``hspace``) go back to *automatic* when set to ``None``.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If a name is not a ``SheetStyle`` field.
    ValueError
        If a value is invalid. Nothing is changed in that case.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.config_layout(width_in=13.33, height_in=7.5, scale="fit")
    >>> sheet.config_layout(wspace=None)        # back to col_gap_in
    """
    valid = {item.name for item in fields(SheetStyle)}
    unknown = sorted(set(changes) - valid)
    if unknown:
        raise TypeError(
            f"Unknown layout option(s): {unknown}. "
            f"Valid options: {sorted(valid)}."
        )

    self._style = replace(self._style, **changes)
    return self

    subplots_adjust(left: float | None = None, bottom: float | None = None, right: float | None = None, top: float | None = None, wspace: float | None = None, hspace: float | None = None) -> Self

    Position the grid of panels, like matplotlib.pyplot.subplots_adjust.

    Only the values you pass are changed. Every value is a fraction:

    • left, right: edges of the grid, as a fraction of the image width (0 is the left border).
    • bottom, top: edges of the grid, as a fraction of the image height measured from the bottom (top=0.9 leaves 10% above the grid). They need a fixed height_in.
    • wspace, hspace: space between columns / rows, as a fraction of the average column width / average row height.

    Anything not set stays automatic: the grid fills the width between margin_in margins, sits between the sheet title and the sources, and uses col_gap_in / row_gap_in as spacing. To go back to automatic use config_layout(left=None, ...).

    Only the values you pass are changed. Every value is a *fraction*:

    * ``left``, ``right``: edges of the grid, as a fraction of the
      image width (0 is the left border).
    * ``bottom``, ``top``: edges of the grid, as a fraction of the
      image height measured **from the bottom** (``top=0.9`` leaves
      10% above the grid). They need a fixed ``height_in``.
    * ``wspace``, ``hspace``: space between columns / rows, as a
      fraction of the average column width / average row height.

    Anything not set stays *automatic*: the grid fills the width
    between ``margin_in`` margins, sits between the sheet title and the
    sources, and uses ``col_gap_in`` / ``row_gap_in`` as spacing. To go
    back to automatic use ``config_layout(left=None, ...)``.

    The sheet title and the sources are aligned to the left edge of the
    grid.

    Parameters
    ----------
    left, bottom, right, top : float | None, default None
        Edges of the grid (0-1).
    wspace, hspace : float | None, default None
        Spacing between panels (>= 0).

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError

        range. Using ``top``/``bottom`` without ``height_in`` raises
        when the sheet is rendered.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.config_layout(width_in=13.33, height_in=7.5)
    >>> sheet.subplots_adjust(left=0.06, right=0.94, top=0.82, bottom=0.12,
    ...                       wspace=0.15, hspace=0.25)
    """
    given = {
        "left": left,
        "bottom": bottom,
        "right": right,
        "top": top,
        "wspace": wspace,
        "hspace": hspace,
    }
    return self.config_layout(
        **{name: value for name, value in given.items() if value is not None}
    )

    layout ¶

    layout(rows: Sequence[Sequence[Key | None]] | None = None, *, nrows: int | None = None, ncols: int | None = None, width_ratios: Sequence[float] | None = None) -> Self

    Arrange the panels on a grid.

    With no arguments the panels are stacked vertically (one per row), which is the default. Panels can be arranged in three ways:

    • nrows / ncols: fill a grid row by row in creation order.
    • rows: an explicit grid, like matplotlib.pyplot.subplot_mosaic. Repeat a panel to make it span several cells; use None or "." for an empty cell. A shorter row is stretched when its length divides the number of columns.
    • width_ratios: relative width of each column.

    Row heights follow the content of each row.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    rows Sequence[Sequence[int | str | None]] | None

    Explicit grid of panel names or positions.

    		 None
    nrows int | None

    Shape of the automatic grid. If only one is given the other is the smallest that holds every panel. Cells left over stay empty. Cannot be combined with rows.

    		 None
    ncols int | None

    Shape of the automatic grid. If only one is given the other is the smallest that holds every panel. Cells left over stay empty. Cannot be combined with rows.

    		 None
    width_ratios Sequence[float] | None

    Relative column widths. Needs one value per column.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    TableSheet

    The sheet, for chaining.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If rows and nrows/ncols are combined, a value is invalid, a panel repeats in cells that do not form a rectangle, or a row cannot be stretched evenly.
    KeyError

    If a panel does not exist.

    Examples:

    >>> sheet.layout()                           # vertical (default)
>>> sheet.layout(nrows=1)                    # horizontal: one row
>>> sheet.layout(ncols=2)                    # two columns
>>> sheet.layout(nrows=2)                    # two rows
>>> sheet.layout([["a", "b"], ["c", "c"]])   # c spans both columns
>>> sheet.layout([["a", "c"], ["b", "c"]], width_ratios=[1, 2])
>>> sheet.layout([["a", "b", "c"], ["d", "d", "e"]])

    rows: Sequence[Sequence[Key | None]] | None = None,
    *,
    nrows: int | None = None,
    ncols: int | None = None,
    width_ratios: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Arrange the panels on a grid.

    With no arguments the panels are stacked vertically (one per row),
    which is the default. Panels can be arranged in three ways:

    * ``nrows`` / ``ncols``: fill a grid row by row in creation order.
    * ``rows``: an explicit grid, like ``matplotlib.pyplot.subplot_mosaic``.
      Repeat a panel to make it span several cells; use ``None`` or
      ``"."`` for an empty cell. A shorter row is stretched when its
      length divides the number of columns.
    * ``width_ratios``: relative width of each column.

    Row heights follow the content of each row.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rows : Sequence[Sequence[int | str | None]] | None, default None
        Explicit grid of panel names or positions.
    nrows, ncols : int | None, default None
        Shape of the automatic grid. If only one is given the other is
        the smallest that holds every panel. Cells left over stay
        empty. Cannot be combined with ``rows``.
    width_ratios : Sequence[float] | None, default None
        Relative column widths. Needs one value per column.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``rows`` and ``nrows``/``ncols`` are combined, a value is
        invalid, a panel repeats in cells that do not form a
        rectangle, or a row cannot be stretched evenly.
    KeyError
        If a panel does not exist.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.layout()                           # vertical (default)
    >>> sheet.layout(nrows=1)                    # horizontal: one row
    >>> sheet.layout(ncols=2)                    # two columns
    >>> sheet.layout(nrows=2)                    # two rows
    >>> sheet.layout([["a", "b"], ["c", "c"]])   # c spans both columns
    >>> sheet.layout([["a", "c"], ["b", "c"]], width_ratios=[1, 2])
    >>> sheet.layout([["a", "b", "c"], ["d", "d", "e"]])
    """
    if rows is not None and (nrows is not None or ncols is not None):
        raise ValueError(
            "Use either rows (explicit grid) or nrows/ncols, not both."
        )
    for label, value in (("nrows", nrows), ("ncols", ncols)):
        if value is not None and (not isinstance(value, int) or value < 1):
            raise ValueError(f"{label} must be an integer >= 1.")

    ratios = None
    if width_ratios is not None:
        ratios = [float(value) for value in width_ratios]
        if any(value <= 0 for value in ratios):
            raise ValueError("width_ratios must be > 0.")

    if rows is None:
        self._mosaic = None
        self._shape = (
            (nrows, ncols) if nrows is not None or ncols is not None else None
        )
        self._width_ratios = ratios
        return self

    if isinstance(rows, (str, int)):
        raise TypeError(
            "rows must be a sequence of sequences, e.g. [['a', 'b'], ['c']]."
        )

    cells: list[list[str | None]] = []
    for row in rows:
        if isinstance(row, (str, int)):
            raise TypeError(
                "rows must be a sequence of sequences, e.g. "
                "[['a', 'b'], ['c']]."
            )
        if not len(row):
            raise ValueError("A layout row cannot be empty.")
        cells.append(
            [
                None
                if key is None or key == EMPTY_CELL
                else self._find(key).name
                for key in row
            ]
        )

    grid = GridLayout.from_rows(cells, ratios)  # validates everything
    self._mosaic = grid.cells
    self._shape = None
    self._width_ratios = ratios
    return self

    def _record(
    self,
    label: str,
    func: StylerFunc,
    *args: Any,
    _expects_styles: bool = False,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Self:
    """
    Append an operation to every active table, atomically.

    If the operation fails on any panel it is removed from all of
    them and the error is re-raised with the panel name attached.

    Parameters
    ----------
    label : str
        Name shown by ``recipe``.
    func : Callable
        ``func(styler, *args, **kwargs)`` returning a ``Styler``.
    _expects_styles : bool, default False
        For operations selecting rows or columns by label: warn when
        the operation added no CSS at all, which means that none of
        the labels matched (the underlying selectors ignore unknown
        labels silently).
    """
    panels = self._targets(tables_only=True)
    done = []

    for panel in panels:
        before = (
            len(panel.build_styler().table_styles or [])
            if _expects_styles
            else 0
        )

        panel.ops.append(Op(label, func, args, dict(kwargs)))
        done.append(panel)
        try:
            built = panel.build_styler()
        except Exception as error:
            for item in done:
                item.ops.pop()
            if hasattr(error, "add_note"):
                error.add_note(
                    f"while applying {label!r} to panel {panel.name!r}"
                )
            raise

        if _expects_styles and len(built.table_styles or []) <= before:
            warnings.warn(
                f"{label} matched nothing on panel {panel.name!r}; "
                "check the labels.",
                stacklevel=3,
            )
    return self

    def _warn_unmatched_style_table(
    self,
    row_index_styles: Sequence[IndexStyleConfig] | None,
    column_header_styles: Sequence[HeaderStyleConfig] | None,
) -> None:
    """Warn about targeted ``style_table`` rules that match nothing."""
    for panel in self._targets(tables_only=True):
        data = panel.build_styler().data

        for config in row_index_styles or ():
            if not get_index_value_selectors(
                df=data,
                values=config["values"],
                level=config["level"],
                parent=config.get("parent"),
            ):
                warnings.warn(
                    f"row_index_styles {config['values']!r} matched "
                    f"nothing on panel {panel.name!r}; check the "
                    "values, level and parent.",
                    stacklevel=3,
                )

        for config in column_header_styles or ():
            if not get_column_header_selectors(
                df=data,
                columns=config["columns"],
                header_level=config.get("level"),
            ):
                warnings.warn(
                    f"column_header_styles {config['columns']!r} "
                    f"matched nothing on panel {panel.name!r}; check "
                    "the columns and level.",
                    stacklevel=3,
                )

    def clear_styles(self) -> Self:
    """
    Remove every recorded operation from the active tables.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.
    """
    for panel in self._targets(tables_only=True):
        panel.ops.clear()
    return self

    def recipe(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """
    Describe the recorded operations of every table.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, list[str]]
        Operation labels, in order, by panel name.
    """
    return {
        panel.name: [op.label for op in panel.ops]
        for panel in self._panels
        if panel.kind == "table"
    }

    style_table ¶

    style_table(font_family: str | None = None, font_size: str | int | float | None = None, text_color: str | None = None, background_color: str | None = None, text_align: str | None = None, header_styles: CSSProperties | None = None, index_styles: CSSProperties | None = None, data_styles: CSSProperties | None = None, column_header_styles: Sequence[HeaderStyleConfig] | None = None, row_index_styles: Sequence[IndexStyleConfig] | None = None, show_index_names: bool = True, corner_styles: CSSProperties | None = None) -> Self

    Configure the general appearance of the active tables.

    Every argument is optional: only the ones you pass are applied. Dictionaries hold plain CSS properties, for example {"background-color": "#12275A", "font-weight": "bold"}. Calling style_table several times is fine: the rules are replayed in call order, so the latest call wins.

    Inside one call the rules are applied in this order. When two of them set the same CSS property, the later one wins (a color in column_header_styles beats one in header_styles):

    1. font_family, font_size, text_color, background_color, text_align: header, index and data cells.
    2. header_styles, index_styles, data_styles: every cell of that kind.
    3. column_header_styles: selected column headers.
    4. row_index_styles: selected row-index labels.
    5. corner_styles: the corner and the index-names row.

    Sparse MultiIndex rendering is preserved. See helpers_ps.DfStyling.style_table for the functional version.

    Parts of a table

    ::

    +----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
| corner   | corner   | corner   |  1M   |  3M   |  <- column headers
+----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
| Metric   | Period   | Rating   |       |       |  <- index-names row
+----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
| Δ Yield  | MTD      | AAA      |   5   |   8   |
|          |          | AA+      |  -9   |  39   |
+----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
  ^ index cells                    ^ data cells
    • Column headers: header_styles, column_header_styles.
    • Index cells (all levels): index_styles, row_index_styles.
    • Data cells: data_styles.
    • Corner cells and index-names row: corner_styles. The index-names row is hidden by show_index_names=False.

    The outline of the whole table and the line between the column headers and the data are not part of style_table: use table_border and header_line.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    font_family str | None

    CSS font family of the header, index and data cells. A list is a fallback chain, e.g. "Inter, Arial, sans-serif". The titles, notes and sources drawn around the table use the sheet font instead (config_layout(font_family=...)).

    		 None
    font_size str | int | float | None

    Font size of the header, index and data cells. A number means pixels (11 is "11px"); a string may use any CSS unit ("9pt", "0.8rem"). With scale="natural" the size on the page is real (1 px = 0.75 pt, so 11 px = 8.25 pt). With the default scale="uniform" the table is resized to fill its cell, so font_size barely changes the final text size; it changes how heavy fixed-pixel borders look next to the text.

    		 None
    text_color str | None

    Text color of the header, index and data cells.

    		 None
    background_color str | None

    Background color of the header, index and data cells. It also covers the alternating row shading (zebra).

    		 None
    text_align str | None

    "left", "center" or "right" for the header, index and data cells. Without it the table is right-aligned.

    		 None
    header_styles Mapping[str, str] | None

    CSS for every column-header cell (the labels above the data). Header labels are bold by default; use {"font-weight": "normal"} to undo it. It does not reach the corner cells; use corner_styles.

    		 None
    index_styles Mapping[str, str] | None

    CSS for every row-index cell, at all index levels. Index labels are bold by default, like the headers.

    		 None
    data_styles Mapping[str, str] | None

    CSS for every data cell.

    		 None
    column_header_styles Sequence[dict] | None

    Rules for selected column headers. Each dictionary has:

    • "columns": one column label or a list of labels. With MultiIndex columns use complete labels as tuples. To style a group label of an upper level, the list must include the first column of that group (the one that carries the label).
    • "styles": the CSS to apply.
    • "level" (optional): header row to style. Default is the last one, the row of the labels closest to the data.
    		 None
    row_index_styles Sequence[dict] | None

    Rules for selected row-index labels. Each dictionary has:

    • "values": one index value or a list of values.
    • "level": index level, as a position (0 is the outer level) or as its name ("Period").
    • "styles": the CSS to apply.
    • "parent" (optional): tuple with the values of the outer levels, to style a repeated label only inside one section.
    		 None
    show_index_names bool

    Show the row with the index level names (Metric, Period, Rating). False hides it without changing the DataFrame.

    		 True
    corner_styles Mapping[str, str] | None

    CSS for the corner cells above the index and for the index-names row, including its empty cells under the column headers.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    TableSheet

    The sheet, for chaining.
    Notes
    • A value that does not exist in the table matches nothing and is ignored.
    • The header row is as tall as its tallest cell, corner included. If you lower the padding or font size of the header, give corner_styles the same values or the row stays tall. In the same way, a data row is as tall as its tallest cell, index included.
    • row_index_styles paints the index label only. To style the data cells of a row use highlight_rows or style_cells.

    Examples:

    The examples use a table with the index levels Metric (Δ Yield, Δ Spreads), Period (MTD, YTD) and Rating (AAA, AA+, AA, A), and the columns 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y.

    font_family.

    >>> sheet.style_table(font_family="Inter, Arial, sans-serif")

    font_size: a number is pixels, a string can use any CSS unit.

    >>> sheet.style_table(font_size=11)
>>> sheet.style_table(font_size="9pt")

    text_color and background_color.

    >>> sheet.style_table(text_color="#222222", background_color="white")

    text_align: centered labels, right-aligned numbers (the data rule is applied after the general one).

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     text_align="center",
...     data_styles={"text-align": "right"},
... )

    header_styles: dark header with white text.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     header_styles={
...         "color": "white",
...         "background-color": "#12275A",
...     },
... )

    index_styles: normal-weight index labels (bold is the default) on a grey background.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     index_styles={
...         "font-weight": "normal",
...         "background-color": "#F2F2F2",
...     },
... )

    data_styles: a thin line under every row.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     data_styles={"border-bottom": "1px solid #E5E5E5"},
... )

    Shorter rows: lower the padding in the data cells and in the index cells, because the tallest cell sets the row height.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     data_styles={"padding": "0.25em 0.6em"},
...     index_styles={"padding": "0.25em 0.6em"},
... )

    column_header_styles: color some headers differently. The general header_styles applies to all of them and the rules of the list are applied after it.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     header_styles={"color": "white", "background-color": "#12275A"},
...     column_header_styles=[
...         {
...             "columns": ["1M", "3M", "6M"],
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#3075DB"},
...         },
...         {
...             "columns": "10Y",
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F"},
...         },
...     ],
... )

    column_header_styles with MultiIndex columns, for example ("Yield", "1M"), ("Yield", "3M"), ("Spread", "1M") and ("Spread", "3M"). "level": 0 styles the group label (Yield), so list the group's columns starting with its first one; without "level" the rule styles the last level (1M, 3M).

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     column_header_styles=[
...         {
...             "columns": [("Yield", "1M"), ("Yield", "3M")],
...             "level": 0,
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
...         },
...         {
...             "columns": [("Spread", "1M"), ("Spread", "3M")],
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#3075DB", "color": "white"},
...         },
...     ],
... )

    row_index_styles: the outer label, the labels of one section (parent) and every AAA of a level selected by name.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     row_index_styles=[
...         {
...             "values": "Δ Yield",
...             "level": 0,
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
...         },
...         {
...             "values": ["MTD", "YTD"],
...             "level": 1,
...             "parent": ("Δ Yield",),
...             "styles": {"font-style": "italic"},
...         },
...         {
...             "values": "AAA",
...             "level": "Rating",
...             "styles": {"color": "#B7331F"},
...         },
...     ],
... )

    show_index_names: hide the Metric / Period / Rating row.

    >>> sheet.style_table(show_index_names=False)

    corner_styles: paint the corner like the header, and keep the header row short by giving the corner the same padding.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     header_styles={
...         "color": "white",
...         "background-color": "#12275A",
...         "padding": "0.2em 0.5em",
...     },
...     corner_styles={
...         "background-color": "#12275A",
...         "padding": "0.2em 0.5em",
...     },
...     show_index_names=False,
... )

    Everything together: an institutional table.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
...     font_family="Inter, Arial",
...     font_size=11,
...     text_align="center",
...     header_styles={"color": "white", "background-color": "#12275A"},
...     corner_styles={"background-color": "#12275A"},
...     index_styles={"background-color": "#F2F2F2"},
...     data_styles={"border-bottom": "1px solid #E5E5E5"},
...     row_index_styles=[
...         {
...             "values": "Δ Yield",
...             "level": 0,
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
...         },
...         {
...             "values": "Δ Spreads",
...             "level": 0,
...             "styles": {"background-color": "#163A87", "color": "white"},
...         },
...     ],
...     show_index_names=False,
... )

    def style_table(
    self,
    font_family: str | None = None,
    font_size: str | int | float | None = None,
    text_color: str | None = None,
    background_color: str | None = None,
    text_align: str | None = None,
    header_styles: CSSProperties | None = None,
    index_styles: CSSProperties | None = None,
    data_styles: CSSProperties | None = None,
    column_header_styles: Sequence[HeaderStyleConfig] | None = None,
    row_index_styles: Sequence[IndexStyleConfig] | None = None,
    show_index_names: bool = True,
    corner_styles: CSSProperties | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Configure the general appearance of the active tables.

    Every argument is optional: only the ones you pass are applied.
    Dictionaries hold plain CSS properties, for example
    ``{"background-color": "#12275A", "font-weight": "bold"}``. Calling
    ``style_table`` several times is fine: the rules are replayed in
    call order, so the latest call wins.

    Inside one call the rules are applied in this order. When two of
    them set the same CSS property, the later one wins (a color in
    ``column_header_styles`` beats one in ``header_styles``):

    1. ``font_family``, ``font_size``, ``text_color``,
       ``background_color``, ``text_align``: header, index and data
       cells.
    2. ``header_styles``, ``index_styles``, ``data_styles``: every cell
       of that kind.
    3. ``column_header_styles``: selected column headers.
    4. ``row_index_styles``: selected row-index labels.
    5. ``corner_styles``: the corner and the index-names row.

    Sparse MultiIndex rendering is preserved. See
    ``helpers_ps.DfStyling.style_table`` for the functional version.

    Parts of a table
    ----------------
    ::

        +----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
        | corner   | corner   | corner   |  1M   |  3M   |  <- column headers
        +----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
        | Metric   | Period   | Rating   |       |       |  <- index-names row
        +----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
        | Δ Yield  | MTD      | AAA      |   5   |   8   |
        |          |          | AA+      |  -9   |  39   |
        +----------+----------+----------+-------+-------+
          ^ index cells                    ^ data cells

    * Column headers: ``header_styles``, ``column_header_styles``.
    * Index cells (all levels): ``index_styles``, ``row_index_styles``.
    * Data cells: ``data_styles``.
    * Corner cells and index-names row: ``corner_styles``. The
      index-names row is hidden by ``show_index_names=False``.

    The outline of the whole table and the line between the column
    headers and the data are not part of ``style_table``: use
    ``table_border`` and ``header_line``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    font_family : str | None, default None
        CSS font family of the header, index and data cells. A list is
        a fallback chain, e.g. ``"Inter, Arial, sans-serif"``. The
        titles, notes and sources drawn around the table use the sheet
        font instead (``config_layout(font_family=...)``).

    font_size : str | int | float | None, default None
        Font size of the header, index and data cells. A number means
        pixels (``11`` is ``"11px"``); a string may use any CSS unit
        (``"9pt"``, ``"0.8rem"``). With ``scale="natural"`` the size on
        the page is real (1 px = 0.75 pt, so 11 px = 8.25 pt). With the
        default ``scale="uniform"`` the table is resized to fill its
        cell, so ``font_size`` barely changes the final text size; it
        changes how heavy fixed-pixel borders look next to the text.

    text_color : str | None, default None
        Text color of the header, index and data cells.

    background_color : str | None, default None
        Background color of the header, index and data cells. It also
        covers the alternating row shading (``zebra``).

    text_align : str | None, default None
        ``"left"``, ``"center"`` or ``"right"`` for the header, index
        and data cells. Without it the table is right-aligned.

    header_styles : Mapping[str, str] | None, default None
        CSS for every column-header cell (the labels above the data).
        Header labels are bold by default; use
        ``{"font-weight": "normal"}`` to undo it. It does not reach the
        corner cells; use ``corner_styles``.

    index_styles : Mapping[str, str] | None, default None
        CSS for every row-index cell, at all index levels. Index labels
        are bold by default, like the headers.

    data_styles : Mapping[str, str] | None, default None
        CSS for every data cell.

    column_header_styles : Sequence[dict] | None, default None
        Rules for selected column headers. Each dictionary has:

        * ``"columns"``: one column label or a list of labels. With
          MultiIndex columns use complete labels as tuples. To style a
          group label of an upper level, the list must include the
          first column of that group (the one that carries the label).
        * ``"styles"``: the CSS to apply.
        * ``"level"`` (optional): header row to style. Default is the
          last one, the row of the labels closest to the data.

    row_index_styles : Sequence[dict] | None, default None
        Rules for selected row-index labels. Each dictionary has:

        * ``"values"``: one index value or a list of values.
        * ``"level"``: index level, as a position (``0`` is the outer
          level) or as its name (``"Period"``).
        * ``"styles"``: the CSS to apply.
        * ``"parent"`` (optional): tuple with the values of the outer
          levels, to style a repeated label only inside one section.

    show_index_names : bool, default True
        Show the row with the index level names (``Metric``,
        ``Period``, ``Rating``). ``False`` hides it without changing
        the DataFrame.

    corner_styles : Mapping[str, str] | None, default None
        CSS for the corner cells above the index and for the
        index-names row, including its empty cells under the column
        headers.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Notes
    -----
    * A value that does not exist in the table matches nothing and is
      ignored.
    * The header row is as tall as its tallest cell, corner included.
      If you lower the padding or font size of the header, give
      ``corner_styles`` the same values or the row stays tall. In the
      same way, a data row is as tall as its tallest cell, index
      included.
    * ``row_index_styles`` paints the index label only. To style the
      data cells of a row use ``highlight_rows`` or ``style_cells``.

    Examples
    --------
    The examples use a table with the index levels ``Metric``
    (``Δ Yield``, ``Δ Spreads``), ``Period`` (``MTD``, ``YTD``) and
    ``Rating`` (``AAA``, ``AA+``, ``AA``, ``A``), and the columns
    ``1M``, ``3M``, ``6M``, ``1Y``, ``3Y``, ``5Y``, ``10Y``.

    ``font_family``.

    >>> sheet.style_table(font_family="Inter, Arial, sans-serif")

    ``font_size``: a number is pixels, a string can use any CSS unit.

    >>> sheet.style_table(font_size=11)
    >>> sheet.style_table(font_size="9pt")

    ``text_color`` and ``background_color``.

    >>> sheet.style_table(text_color="#222222", background_color="white")

    ``text_align``: centered labels, right-aligned numbers (the data
    rule is applied after the general one).

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     text_align="center",
    ...     data_styles={"text-align": "right"},
    ... )

    ``header_styles``: dark header with white text.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     header_styles={
    ...         "color": "white",
    ...         "background-color": "#12275A",
    ...     },
    ... )

    ``index_styles``: normal-weight index labels (bold is the default)
    on a grey background.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     index_styles={
    ...         "font-weight": "normal",
    ...         "background-color": "#F2F2F2",
    ...     },
    ... )

    ``data_styles``: a thin line under every row.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     data_styles={"border-bottom": "1px solid #E5E5E5"},
    ... )

    Shorter rows: lower the padding in the data cells and in the index
    cells, because the tallest cell sets the row height.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     data_styles={"padding": "0.25em 0.6em"},
    ...     index_styles={"padding": "0.25em 0.6em"},
    ... )

    ``column_header_styles``: color some headers differently. The
    general ``header_styles`` applies to all of them and the rules of
    the list are applied after it.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     header_styles={"color": "white", "background-color": "#12275A"},
    ...     column_header_styles=[
    ...         {
    ...             "columns": ["1M", "3M", "6M"],
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#3075DB"},
    ...         },
    ...         {
    ...             "columns": "10Y",
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F"},
    ...         },
    ...     ],
    ... )

    ``column_header_styles`` with MultiIndex columns, for example
    ``("Yield", "1M")``, ``("Yield", "3M")``, ``("Spread", "1M")`` and
    ``("Spread", "3M")``. ``"level": 0`` styles the group label
    (``Yield``), so list the group's columns starting with its first
    one; without ``"level"`` the rule styles the last level (``1M``,
    ``3M``).

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     column_header_styles=[
    ...         {
    ...             "columns": [("Yield", "1M"), ("Yield", "3M")],
    ...             "level": 0,
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
    ...         },
    ...         {
    ...             "columns": [("Spread", "1M"), ("Spread", "3M")],
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#3075DB", "color": "white"},
    ...         },
    ...     ],
    ... )

    ``row_index_styles``: the outer label, the labels of one section
    (``parent``) and every ``AAA`` of a level selected by name.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     row_index_styles=[
    ...         {
    ...             "values": "Δ Yield",
    ...             "level": 0,
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
    ...         },
    ...         {
    ...             "values": ["MTD", "YTD"],
    ...             "level": 1,
    ...             "parent": ("Δ Yield",),
    ...             "styles": {"font-style": "italic"},
    ...         },
    ...         {
    ...             "values": "AAA",
    ...             "level": "Rating",
    ...             "styles": {"color": "#B7331F"},
    ...         },
    ...     ],
    ... )

    ``show_index_names``: hide the ``Metric`` / ``Period`` / ``Rating``
    row.

    >>> sheet.style_table(show_index_names=False)

    ``corner_styles``: paint the corner like the header, and keep the
    header row short by giving the corner the same padding.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     header_styles={
    ...         "color": "white",
    ...         "background-color": "#12275A",
    ...         "padding": "0.2em 0.5em",
    ...     },
    ...     corner_styles={
    ...         "background-color": "#12275A",
    ...         "padding": "0.2em 0.5em",
    ...     },
    ...     show_index_names=False,
    ... )

    Everything together: an institutional table.

    >>> sheet.style_table(
    ...     font_family="Inter, Arial",
    ...     font_size=11,
    ...     text_align="center",
    ...     header_styles={"color": "white", "background-color": "#12275A"},
    ...     corner_styles={"background-color": "#12275A"},
    ...     index_styles={"background-color": "#F2F2F2"},
    ...     data_styles={"border-bottom": "1px solid #E5E5E5"},
    ...     row_index_styles=[
    ...         {
    ...             "values": "Δ Yield",
    ...             "level": 0,
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#B7331F", "color": "white"},
    ...         },
    ...         {
    ...             "values": "Δ Spreads",
    ...             "level": 0,
    ...             "styles": {"background-color": "#163A87", "color": "white"},
    ...         },
    ...     ],
    ...     show_index_names=False,
    ... )
    """
    self._record(
        "style_table",
        style_table,
        font_family=font_family,
        font_size=font_size,
        text_color=text_color,
        background_color=background_color,
        text_align=text_align,
        header_styles=header_styles,
        index_styles=index_styles,
        data_styles=data_styles,
        column_header_styles=column_header_styles,
        row_index_styles=row_index_styles,
        show_index_names=show_index_names,
        corner_styles=corner_styles,
    )
    self._warn_unmatched_style_table(
        row_index_styles, column_header_styles
    )
    return self

    """

    Tables have **no outline by default**; call this only if you want
    one. It applies to the active tables.

    ----------

        CSS width, or a number of pixels. See *Line thickness* in

    -------
    TableSheet

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.table_border(color="#12275A")
    >>> sheet.table_border(2, "black", "dashed")
    >>> sheet.table_border(line_style="none")        # remove it again

        style_table_border,

    border_rows ¶

    border_rows(rows: Labels, position: RowBorderPosition = 'bottom', styles: OptionalCSSProperties = None) -> Self

    Add a horizontal border across rows.

    The line is drawn under (or over) the complete HTML row, so it also crosses the merged cells of a sparse MultiIndex. See helpers_ps.DfStyling.border_rows.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    rows label | list of labels

    Row to draw the line under. For a MultiIndex pass the complete tuple, or a list of tuples.

    		 required
    position ('bottom', 'top')

    Side of the row that receives the line.

    		 "bottom"
    styles dict | None

    Any of these options (anything else raises ValueError):

    • "width": a CSS length ("2px") or a number of pixels.
    • "style" (or "line_style"): "solid", "dashed", "dotted", "double"...
    • "color": any CSS color.

    "border-width", "border-style" and "border-color" are accepted as aliases. Defaults: 1px solid black.

    		 None
    Notes

    Line thickness. The browser draws the borders of a table in whole CSS pixels with a minimum of 1px, so "0.1px", "0.5px" and "1px" are the same line and "1.5px" is drawn as "1px" (a warning tells you). The thickness you see is relative to the text:

    line thickness = text size x width / font_size

    The sheet scales the table to fit its cell, so the final text size does not depend on style_table(font_size=...), but the line does. With font_size=3 a 1px line is a third of the height of the text. To get a thinner line, raise font_size; to keep the look of the rest of the table, give sizes inside the table in em instead of px. Measured on a 5.4 in sheet with two tables and text of about 5.3 pt (1px and 2px lines):

    ============ ========= ========= font_size 1px line 2px line ============ ========= ========= 3 1.8 pt 3.5 pt 6 0.9 pt 1.8 pt 12 0.45 pt 0.9 pt 24 0.23 pt 0.46 pt ============ ========= =========

    Examples:

    >>> sheet.border_rows(
...     [("Δ Yield", "MTD", "A")],
...     styles={"width": "2px", "color": "#12275A"},
... )
>>> sheet.border_rows(
...     [("Δ Yield", "MTD", "A"), ("Δ Spreads", "MTD", "A")],
...     styles={"width": 1, "color": "#808080", "line_style": "dashed"},
... )

    def border_rows(
    self,
    rows: Labels,
    position: RowBorderPosition = "bottom",
    styles: OptionalCSSProperties = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a horizontal border across rows.

    The line is drawn under (or over) the complete HTML row, so it also
    crosses the merged cells of a sparse MultiIndex. See
    ``helpers_ps.DfStyling.border_rows``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    rows : label | list of labels
        Row to draw the line under. For a MultiIndex pass the complete
        tuple, or a list of tuples.
    position : {"bottom", "top"}, default "bottom"
        Side of the row that receives the line.
    styles : dict | None, default None
        Any of these options (anything else raises ``ValueError``):

        * ``"width"``: a CSS length (``"2px"``) or a number of pixels.
        * ``"style"`` (or ``"line_style"``): ``"solid"``, ``"dashed"``,
          ``"dotted"``, ``"double"``...
        * ``"color"``: any CSS color.

        ``"border-width"``, ``"border-style"`` and ``"border-color"``
        are accepted as aliases. Defaults: ``1px solid black``.

    Notes
    -----
    **Line thickness.** The browser draws the borders of a table in
    whole CSS pixels with a minimum of 1px, so ``"0.1px"``, ``"0.5px"``
    and ``"1px"`` are the same line and ``"1.5px"`` is drawn as ``"1px"``
    (a warning tells you). The thickness you see is relative to the text:

        line thickness = text size x width / font_size

    The sheet scales the table to fit its cell, so the **final text size
    does not depend on** ``style_table(font_size=...)``, but the line
    does. With ``font_size=3`` a ``1px`` line is a third of the height of
    the text. To get a thinner line, raise ``font_size``; to keep the
    look of the rest of the table, give sizes inside the table in ``em``
    instead of ``px``. Measured on a 5.4 in sheet with two tables and
    text of about 5.3 pt (``1px`` and ``2px`` lines):

    ============  =========  =========
    font_size     1px line   2px line
    ============  =========  =========
    3             1.8 pt     3.5 pt
    6             0.9 pt     1.8 pt
    12            0.45 pt    0.9 pt
    24            0.23 pt    0.46 pt
    ============  =========  =========

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.border_rows(
    ...     [("Δ Yield", "MTD", "A")],
    ...     styles={"width": "2px", "color": "#12275A"},
    ... )
    >>> sheet.border_rows(
    ...     [("Δ Yield", "MTD", "A"), ("Δ Spreads", "MTD", "A")],
    ...     styles={"width": 1, "color": "#808080", "line_style": "dashed"},
    ... )
    """
    return self._record(
        "border_rows",
        border_rows,
        _expects_styles=True,
        rows=rows,
        position=position,
        styles=styles,
    )

    def apply_styler(
    self,
    func: str | StylerFunc,
    *args: Any,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> Self:
    """
    Apply any ``Styler`` operation.

    Parameters
    ----------
    func : str | Callable
        Name of a ``Styler`` method, or a function
        ``func(styler, *args, **kwargs)`` that returns a ``Styler``.
    *args, **kwargs
        Forwarded to the method or function.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.apply_styler("background_gradient", cmap="Blues", axis=None)
    >>> sheet.apply_styler(lambda s: s.set_caption("Daily changes"))
    """
    if isinstance(func, str):
        return self._record(func, _styler_method, func, *args, **kwargs)

    if not callable(func):
        raise TypeError("func must be a Styler method name or a callable.")

    label = getattr(func, "__name__", "custom")
    return self._record(label, func, *args, **kwargs)

    def _new_name(self, name: str | None) -> str:
    if name is None:
        name = f"panel_{self._counter}"
    elif not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
        raise TypeError("A panel name must be a non-empty str.")
    elif name == ".":
        raise ValueError("'.' is reserved for empty layout cells.")

    if any(panel.name == name for panel in self._panels):
        raise ValueError(f"A panel named {name!r} already exists.")

    self._counter += 1
    return name

    def add_table(
    self,
    dataframe: DataFrame | Styler | Series,
    name: str | None = None,
    *,
    activate: bool = True,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a table panel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame | pandas.io.formats.style.Styler | pandas.Series
        Table source. A ``Styler`` is used as the starting point of
        the recipe (it is copied, never modified).
    name : str | None, default None
        Panel name. Defaults to ``"panel_<n>"``.
    activate : bool, default True
        Make the new panel the only active one, so the next styling
        calls apply to it.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet = (
    ...     TableSheet(df_yield, names=["yield"])
    ...     .add_table(df_spreads, name="spreads")
    ...     .style_table(font_size=11)     # applies to "spreads"
    ... )
    """
    if isinstance(dataframe, Series):
        dataframe = dataframe.to_frame()

    if not isinstance(dataframe, (DataFrame, Styler)):
        raise TypeError(
            "dataframe must be a pandas DataFrame, Styler or Series, "
            f"got {type(dataframe).__name__}."
        )

    panel = Panel(
        name=self._new_name(name),
        kind="table",
        source=dataframe,
    )
    self._panels.append(panel)

    if activate:
        self._active = [panel.name]
    return self

    def add_image(
    self,
    image: Any,
    name: str | None = None,
    *,
    activate: bool = True,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add an image panel, typically a chart.

    Parameters
    ----------
    image : numpy.ndarray | PIL.Image.Image | bytes | str | pathlib.Path | matplotlib.figure.Figure | object
        Image source. Figures, and objects exposing one as ``_fig``
        (such as ``GraphMtplt``), are rasterized at render time with
        the sheet ``dpi``, so they always reflect their current state.
        Arrays, PIL images, encoded bytes and file paths are loaded
        immediately.
    name : str | None, default None
        Panel name. Defaults to ``"panel_<n>"``.
    activate : bool, default True
        Make the new panel the only active one.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.add_image(graph, name="curve").panel(title="Yield curve")
    """
    array = load_static_image(image)

    if array is not None:
        source: Any = array
    else:
        source = figure_of(image)
        if source is None:
            raise TypeError(
                "image must be an array, PIL image, bytes, path, "
                "matplotlib Figure or an object with a Figure in "
                f"'_fig', got {type(image).__name__}."
            )

    panel = Panel(
        name=self._new_name(name),
        kind="image",
        source=source,
    )
    self._panels.append(panel)

    if activate:
        self._active = [panel.name]
    return self

    def on(self, *keys: Key) -> Self:
    """
    Select the panels that the next calls apply to.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *keys : int | str
        Panel positions (negative values allowed) or names. With no
        arguments, every panel is selected.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.on("yield").style_table(font_size=11)
    >>> sheet.on("yield", "spreads").style_table(font_family="Arial")
    >>> sheet.on().style_table(text_align="center")       # all panels
    """
    if not self._panels:
        raise ValueError("The sheet has no panels yet.")

    if not keys:
        self._active = [panel.name for panel in self._panels]
    else:
        names: list[str] = []
        for key in keys:
            name = self._find(key).name
            if name not in names:
                names.append(name)
        self._active = names
    return self

    def remove(self, *keys: Key) -> Self:
    """
    Remove panels (and their cells in an explicit layout).

    Rows and columns of an explicit layout that become empty are
    dropped, together with their ``width_ratios``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *keys : int | str
        Panel positions or names.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.
    """
    doomed = {self._find(key).name for key in keys}

    self._panels = [p for p in self._panels if p.name not in doomed]

    if self._mosaic is not None:
        self._mosaic, self._width_ratios = GridLayout.without(
            self._mosaic, self._width_ratios, doomed
        )

    self._active = [name for name in self._active if name not in doomed]
    if not self._active and self._panels:
        self._active = [self._panels[0].name]
    return self

    def panel(
    self,
    *,
    title: str | None = None,
    subtitle: str | None = None,
    notes: Notes = None,
    align: Align | None = None,
    valign: VAlign | None = None,
    scale: ScaleMode | None = None,
    title_size: float | None = None,
    title_color: str | None = None,
    title_weight: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """
    Set texts and geometry of the active panels.

    ``None`` leaves a setting unchanged. Use an empty string (or an
    empty list for ``notes``) to clear it. Column widths are set with
    ``layout(width_ratios=...)``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    title : str | None, default None
        Text above the table.
    subtitle : str | None, default None
        Smaller text under the title.
    notes : str | Sequence[str] | None, default None
        Notes below the table. Replaces the previous ones.
    align : {"left", "center", "right"} | None, default None
        Horizontal alignment when the panel is narrower than its cell.
    valign : {"top", "center", "bottom"} | None, default None
        Vertical alignment when its cell is taller than the panel,
        for example a panel that spans several rows.
    scale : {"uniform", "fit", "natural"} | None, default None
        Overrides the sheet ``scale`` for these panels, e.g.
        ``scale="fit"`` to make a chart fill its cell width.
    title_size, title_color, title_weight : optional
        Overrides of the sheet title style for these panels.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.on("yield").panel(
    ...     title="Δ Yield",
    ...     subtitle="Basis points",
    ...     notes="MTD: month to date.",
    ... )
    >>> sheet.on("curve").panel(scale="fit", valign="center")
    """
    if align is not None and align not in ALIGNS:
        raise ValueError(f"align must be one of {ALIGNS}, got {align!r}.")
    if valign is not None and valign not in VALIGNS:
        raise ValueError(f"valign must be one of {VALIGNS}, got {valign!r}.")
    if scale is not None and scale not in SCALE_MODES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"scale must be one of {SCALE_MODES}, got {scale!r}."
        )

    for panel in self._targets():
        if title is not None:
            panel.title = title
        if subtitle is not None:
            panel.subtitle = subtitle
        if notes is not None:
            panel.notes = _as_list(notes)
        if align is not None:
            panel.align = align
        if valign is not None:
            panel.valign = valign
        if scale is not None:
            panel.scale = scale
        if title_size is not None:
            panel.title_size = title_size
        if title_color is not None:
            panel.title_color = title_color
        if title_weight is not None:
            panel.title_weight = title_weight
    return self

    def add_table(
    self,
    dataframe: DataFrame | Styler | Series,
    name: str | None = None,
    *,
    activate: bool = True,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add a table panel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dataframe : pandas.DataFrame | pandas.io.formats.style.Styler | pandas.Series
        Table source. A ``Styler`` is used as the starting point of
        the recipe (it is copied, never modified).
    name : str | None, default None
        Panel name. Defaults to ``"panel_<n>"``.
    activate : bool, default True
        Make the new panel the only active one, so the next styling
        calls apply to it.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet = (
    ...     TableSheet(df_yield, names=["yield"])
    ...     .add_table(df_spreads, name="spreads")
    ...     .style_table(font_size=11)     # applies to "spreads"
    ... )
    """
    if isinstance(dataframe, Series):
        dataframe = dataframe.to_frame()

    if not isinstance(dataframe, (DataFrame, Styler)):
        raise TypeError(
            "dataframe must be a pandas DataFrame, Styler or Series, "
            f"got {type(dataframe).__name__}."
        )

    panel = Panel(
        name=self._new_name(name),
        kind="table",
        source=dataframe,
    )
    self._panels.append(panel)

    if activate:
        self._active = [panel.name]
    return self

    def add_image(
    self,
    image: Any,
    name: str | None = None,
    *,
    activate: bool = True,
) -> Self:
    """
    Add an image panel, typically a chart.

    Parameters
    ----------
    image : numpy.ndarray | PIL.Image.Image | bytes | str | pathlib.Path | matplotlib.figure.Figure | object
        Image source. Figures, and objects exposing one as ``_fig``
        (such as ``GraphMtplt``), are rasterized at render time with
        the sheet ``dpi``, so they always reflect their current state.
        Arrays, PIL images, encoded bytes and file paths are loaded
        immediately.
    name : str | None, default None
        Panel name. Defaults to ``"panel_<n>"``.
    activate : bool, default True
        Make the new panel the only active one.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.add_image(graph, name="curve").panel(title="Yield curve")
    """
    array = load_static_image(image)

    if array is not None:
        source: Any = array
    else:
        source = figure_of(image)
        if source is None:
            raise TypeError(
                "image must be an array, PIL image, bytes, path, "
                "matplotlib Figure or an object with a Figure in "
                f"'_fig', got {type(image).__name__}."
            )

    panel = Panel(
        name=self._new_name(name),
        kind="image",
        source=source,
    )
    self._panels.append(panel)

    if activate:
        self._active = [panel.name]
    return self

    def on(self, *keys: Key) -> Self:
    """
    Select the panels that the next calls apply to.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *keys : int | str
        Panel positions (negative values allowed) or names. With no
        arguments, every panel is selected.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> sheet.on("yield").style_table(font_size=11)
    >>> sheet.on("yield", "spreads").style_table(font_family="Arial")
    >>> sheet.on().style_table(text_align="center")       # all panels
    """
    if not self._panels:
        raise ValueError("The sheet has no panels yet.")

    if not keys:
        self._active = [panel.name for panel in self._panels]
    else:
        names: list[str] = []
        for key in keys:
            name = self._find(key).name
            if name not in names:
                names.append(name)
        self._active = names
    return self

    def remove(self, *keys: Key) -> Self:
    """
    Remove panels (and their cells in an explicit layout).

    Rows and columns of an explicit layout that become empty are
    dropped, together with their ``width_ratios``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *keys : int | str
        Panel positions or names.

    Returns
    -------
    TableSheet
        The sheet, for chaining.
    """
    doomed = {self._find(key).name for key in keys}

    self._panels = [p for p in self._panels if p.name not in doomed]

    if self._mosaic is not None:
        self._mosaic, self._width_ratios = GridLayout.without(
            self._mosaic, self._width_ratios, doomed
        )

    self._active = [name for name in self._active if name not in doomed]
    if not self._active and self._panels:
        self._active = [self._panels[0].name]
    return self
